beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! Today's a special one.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, you learned about turns. A quarter turn is ninety degrees, and four quarter turns bring you all the way around.
beats.caption: Last time: a quarter turn = 90°

beats.vo: Today is chapter five, the very last chapter of Unit three, Shapes, Grids and Coordinates.
beats.caption: Unit 3 · Chapter 5 · the last one!

beats.vo: It's called, Draw With Math. We're going to draw shapes using only words and numbers.
beats.caption: Chapter 5 · Draw With Math

beats.vo: No pencil in your hand. Just clear commands, like a real programmer. Ready? Let's go!
beats.caption: Draw with commands, like a programmer!

beats.vo: Meet Kachhu. Kachhu is a little robot turtle, with a pen tucked under his tummy. When he walks, he draws a line.
beats.caption: Meet Kachhu, the robot turtle

beats.vo: Your friend Meera puts him on a big sheet of paper, and says, Kachhu, draw a square!
beats.caption: "Kachhu, draw a square!"

beats.vo: And Kachhu just sits there. He doesn't move one bit.
beats.caption: Kachhu doesn't move…

beats.vo: Hmm. Why not? Think about it for a moment.
beats.caption: Why didn't Kachhu draw? Think!

beats.vo: Here's the thing. Kachhu doesn't know what a square is. He only understands a few tiny commands. So we have to tell him, step by step, exactly what to do.
beats.caption: He only understands tiny commands

beats.vo: A command is one clear instruction. Kachhu knows just two of them.
beats.caption: Command = one clear instruction

beats.vo: The first one is, forward. Forward four means, walk four steps straight ahead. His pen is down, so he draws a line as he walks.
beats.caption: forward 4 → walk 4 steps, draw a line

beats.vo: The number tells him how far to go. Forward two makes a short line. Forward eight makes a long one.
beats.caption: The number = how many steps

beats.vo: The second command is, turn right ninety. Remember last chapter? That's a quarter turn, clockwise. Kachhu spins on the spot. He doesn't walk, so no line is drawn.
beats.caption: turn right 90 → spin a quarter turn

beats.vo: So here's the rule. Forward draws. Turning just spins.
beats.caption: Forward draws. Turning spins.

beats.vo: Now, let's draw that square! First, what does a square have? Four equal sides, and four square corners.
beats.caption: A square: 4 equal sides, 4 square corners

beats.vo: So we say, forward four. Kachhu draws the first side. Then, turn right ninety, for the corner.
beats.caption: forward 4, turn right 90 · side 1

beats.vo: Again! Forward four, turn right ninety. That's side two. And again. Forward four, turn right ninety. Side three.
beats.caption: Again… side 2. Again… side 3

beats.vo: One last time. Forward four, turn right ninety. Look! The lines meet, and Kachhu is back where he started, facing the same way.
beats.caption: Side 4 · back to the start!

beats.vo: Four sides, four corners. A perfect square! We did forward four, turn right ninety, four times.
beats.caption: 4 times: forward 4, turn right 90

beats.vo: But writing all eight lines is a lot of work. Phew!
beats.caption: 8 lines… that's a lot!

beats.vo: So programmers use a shortcut, called repeat. Repeat four, forward four, turn right ninety. It means, do these two commands, four times.
beats.caption: repeat 4 [forward 4, turn right 90]

beats.vo: In coding, this is called a loop. Do it, and again, and again.
beats.caption: Repeat = a loop

beats.vo: And a list of commands that a computer follows in order? That's a program. So you just wrote a tiny program! How cool is that?
beats.caption: Commands in order = a tiny program!

beats.vo: Now Meera wants a bigger square. Which number should we change? Have a think.
beats.caption: Bigger square? Which number changes?

beats.vo: Just the forward number! Change forward four, into forward eight. Every side gets twice as long.
beats.caption: forward 4 → forward 8

beats.vo: But keep turn right ninety, and keep repeat four. A square always needs four square corners. Turn only forty-five, and you won't get a square at all!
beats.caption: Keep turn right 90 and repeat 4

beats.vo: Let's count how far Kachhu walks. Four sides, with four steps each. Four times four, equals sixteen steps.
beats.caption: 4 sides × 4 steps = 16 steps

beats.vo: And the big square? Four sides of eight steps. That's thirty-two steps!
beats.caption: 4 sides × 8 steps = 32 steps

beats.vo: What about a rectangle? It has two long sides, and two short sides. Let's make it six steps long, and three steps tall.
beats.caption: Rectangle: long side 6, short side 3

beats.vo: Forward six, turn right ninety. Forward three, turn right ninety. That's half of it.
beats.caption: forward 6, turn, forward 3, turn

beats.vo: Do that two times, and it's done! Repeat two. Forward six, turn right ninety, forward three, turn right ninety.
beats.caption: repeat 2 [forward 6, turn, forward 3, turn]

beats.vo: So how many steps does Kachhu walk this time? Try adding it up.
beats.caption: How many steps in total?

beats.vo: Six, plus three, plus six, plus three. That's eighteen steps!
beats.caption: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 steps

beats.vo: Here's a fun one. A plus sign! Kachhu starts in the middle, and learns one new command. Back, which means walk backwards.
beats.caption: Plus sign · new command: back

beats.vo: Forward two, back two, turn right ninety. That draws one arm, and brings him back to the middle.
beats.caption: forward 2, back 2, turn right 90

beats.vo: Repeat that four times, and you get four arms. A plus sign!
beats.caption: repeat 4 → 4 arms → a plus sign!

beats.vo: Uh oh. Meera wrote a square program, but Kachhu drew something strange.
beats.caption: Uh-oh! A broken square

beats.vo: Forward four, turn right ninety. Three times. Only three sides! What's the bug? How would you fix it?
beats.caption: Only 3 sides. How do you fix it?

beats.vo: Add one more forward four! That draws the missing side. Checking each command in order to find the mistake? That's debugging.
beats.caption: Fix: add one more forward 4

beats.vo: One more puzzle. Kachhu faces north, towards the top. He does forward two, turn right ninety, two times. Which way is he facing now?
beats.caption: Faces north · forward 2, right 90 · twice

beats.vo: South! The first turn takes him from north to east. The second, from east to south. Two quarter turns make a half turn.
beats.caption: North → East → South

beats.vo: Okay champ, your turn to be the programmer! Here's a practice check, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: Write the commands to draw a square, with four steps on each side. Pause the video, and try it on paper.
beats.caption: Write commands: a square, 4 steps a side

beats.vo: Here's one way. Forward four, turn right ninety, and do it four times. Or the short way. Repeat four, forward four, turn right ninety. Brilliant!
beats.caption: repeat 4 [forward 4, turn right 90]

beats.vo: Let's remember. A square is, repeat four, forward, then turn right ninety.
beats.caption: Square = repeat 4 [forward, turn right 90]

beats.vo: Change the forward number, to change the size.
beats.caption: Forward number = the size

beats.vo: Forward draws. Turning just spins on the spot.
beats.caption: Forward draws. Turning spins.

beats.vo: And commands in order make a tiny program.
beats.caption: Commands in order = a tiny program

beats.vo: Chapter five, done! And that means all of Unit three is complete! Shapes, grids, symmetry, turns, and now drawing with commands. Wow, champ!
beats.caption: Chapter 5 done · Unit 3 complete!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
